what_happened: Scope correction recorded at creation time, before any research dispatch: this task's title says 'seven' red Gate 8 suites and its file_scope lists test-gate-lock.sh, but test-gate-lock.sh was fixed and verified green (16 passed, 0 failed, EXIT=0, confirmed by an isolated re-run) by the same conclusion stage's channel-(a) direct-fix dispatch, commit 7421bdceb, which added a signal-scoped INT/TERM/HUP trap around gate8_run()'s mutex-owning window in verify-deploy.sh. The true count of remaining red suites is therefore SIX, not seven: test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh, test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh, test-orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh, test-orchestrate-unwind-dispatch.sh, test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh, test-redeploy-checkpoint-promotion.sh. test-gate-lock.sh is retained in file_scope deliberately rather than removed: update-task-status.sh's --file-scope-add is additive-only with no sanctioned remove, and an over-broad file_scope errs toward more serialization, which is the safe direction. Of the six remaining, five (cycle-postflight, predispatch-review, unwind-dispatch, postflight-deploy-gate, redeploy-checkpoint-promotion) were proven to fail identically on unmodified master via git stash push, and test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh plus test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh are already EXPECTED-baselined by run-all.sh itself. test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh was separately re-run in isolation: 14 passed, 1 failed, with the sole failure being a fixture-setup self-check reporting 'baseline fixture is not clean (rc=1, gate20 finding lines=0)' -- a host/repo-state leak into the fixture, not a Gate 20 ceiling defect.

Corroborating evidence from a later batch's own full verify-deploy run (session sess_1793993117_98582a, 8 tasks, all completed): gate 8 confirmed NINE failing suites, this record's seven plus test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh (already owned by the context-budget byte-count-drift record, correctly excluded here) and test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh, which is NOT in this record's declared file_scope and has no other owner. Provenance check on all nine: eight were last touched by other in-flight records and none by the observing batch -- the systematic script-and-test corpus consolidation record's harness migration tranche c accounts for five of them (test-gate-lock, test-orchestrate-unwind-dispatch, test-postflight-deploy-gate, test-redeploy-checkpoint-promotion, test-verify-deploy-context-budget), the explicit lint-fixture subject-resolution record for test-lint-unit-integration-boundary, the WORK (h) postflight migration for test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight, and the dirty-file-scope advisory record for test-orchestrate-predispatch-review. Only test-gate-cache-equivalence was touched by the observing batch. STRONG HINT FOR THIS RECORD'S RESEARCH: a prior investigation root-caused a cluster of five gate-8 failures to ONE shared foreign cause (fixture library-requirement lists predating a new library dependency in a shared lib) rather than five independent bugs. Grep the nine suites for a shared miss before treating them as nine defects. Separately measured: test-gate-cache-equivalence itself drives a full verify-deploy pass and exceeded 300s standalone under load, so it is slow by construction, not merely red.

All seven of this task's in-scope suites now pass standalone with zero failures (test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh 17/0, test-gate-lock.sh 16/0, test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh 312/0, test-orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh 37/0, test-orchestrate-unwind-dispatch.sh 21/0, test-postflight-deploy-gate.sh 29/0, test-redeploy-checkpoint-promotion.sh 17/0), and both declared dependencies (423, 445) plus a third task (568) that independently fixed one of the five shared-cause suites are all closed. Report 01's suggested fixture-allowlist remedy is already applied upstream by commit a4e32ff9e and at least one other not-yet-identified commit. Remaining task scope is much smaller than the dispatch description assumes.

test-gate-lock.sh passes standalone (16 passed, 0 failed) but fails with 14 passed, 2 failed when run via run-all.sh --only alongside its six file-scope siblings; run-all.sh --fail-on-new classifies it NEW (no known-failures.txt row exists). Both failing cases (killed holder process-group teardown; fail-open verify-deploy.sh Gate 8) are timing/host-load-coupled per shell-script-testing.md's Ambient-host-state isolation section. Root cause not fully isolated in this research dispatch; see report 02 Finding 4 for the two candidate mechanisms and exact reproduction command.

The dispatch's instruction to hand the test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh fixture-not-clean finding (rc=1, gate20 finding lines=0) to record 423 cannot be discharged literally: 423 closed 2026-11-10 with a different root-cause attribution (gate-24 /ide findings), and this symptom reproduces verbatim right now even after a later commit (a4e32ff9e) specifically touched this suite's fixture. This suite is outside 476's file_scope by deliberate design; a new follow-up task is needed since 423 cannot receive new findings. Not actioned here per scope.

The prior research dispatch's premise-refresh report (reports/02) let this plan dispatch re-scope the task away from the dispatch description's superseded framing (seven red suites, two open blocking dependencies) onto the three items that are actually still outstanding, with zero re-measurement needed in the plan phase. Running suite_selection_select over each phase's Files to modify paths produced honest Tier Justification suite lists directly, with no guessing.

Classified test-gate-lock.sh's two aggregate-only failing cases (report 02 Finding 4: 14 passed/2 failed, matched to known-failures.txt-free NEW status) as class (a) ambient-host-state leak into the suite's own fixture timing, not class (c)/(d). Evidence: (1) the plan's own reproduction command (--only with the 6 non-gate-cache-equivalence siblings, --fail-on-new) was run 3 times and report02's own exact 7-suite command pattern was matched in mechanism; all 3 attempts passed 6/6 clean, 0 failures -- the original 14/2 did not re-reproduce under today's host load (load average 6.19/8.52/10.62 on 24 cores, moderate not idle). (2) Live-code analysis of run-all.sh (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/run-all.sh lines 774-781) confirms test-gate-lock.sh is in LOAD_SENSITIVE_BASENAMES (added at suite creation, commit 8d7ea97e7, 2026-10-18 -- predates this task's research), which runs it fully serially BEFORE the parallel pool starts (lines 900-914): it can never overlap with sibling suites inside one run-all.sh invocation. This refutes the literal 'fails when run concurrently with its file-scope siblings' framing; the real trigger must be external ambient host load at measurement time, not intra-run-all.sh sibling contention. (3) A diagnostic instrumented copy (_diag-gate-lock.sh, deleted after use, never committed) of the suite's 'killed holder (process-group teardown)' case, run 3x standalone, measured pid-appear and lockdir-appear at 50ms (vs 3000ms poll budget) and lockdir-gone plus full process death at 500ms/0ms (vs 3000ms budget) -- generous headroom under today's conditions, consistent with the case being a real but currently-unhit timing-margin risk rather than a deterministic defect. (4) The carried speculation that a concurrent sibling's in-flight edit to update-task-status.sh causes this was discarded: the suite's own REQUIRED file list (lines 56-58) and fixture copy-list (lines 87-93) never reference update-task-status.sh or any file in its dependency chain, and verify-deploy.sh's gate8_run() path does not invoke it either -- there is no causal path for that speculation to apply. (5) Could not force-reproduce the 'fail-open (verify-deploy.sh Gate 8)' exit-2 case at all in 6 total attempts (3 plain aggregate + 3 diagnostic standalone), so the specific exit-2 site (zero-suites-discovered vs TOTAL_ACCOUNTED mismatch) was not directly isolated; this remains unconfirmed. Judged, from the shared- mechanics, that the two cases most plausibly share ONE cause (the teardown case's backgrounded setsid child's death being inferred only from GATE_LOCK_DIR's disappearance, not confirmed via PID liveness, leaving a window for a still-winding-down child to pollute the next case including fail-open-vd's reuse of the same $WORKDIR) rather than two independent causes, though this is inference from mechanism, not a captured second occurrence.

Phase 2's plan called for removing test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh's known-failures.txt row as stale (both suites it named -- test-mcp-merge-target.sh, test-validate-no-python-state-write.sh -- now have classification rows). Confirmed those two ARE fixed, but direct standalone re-run showed the suite is still red (14 passed, 1 failed), for a DIFFERENT, newly-discovered coverage gap: test-gate8-suite-selection.sh (added to the corpus by a separate, already-committed change, without a suite-classification.data edit) has no classification row. Per the plan's own Scope Hypothesis guidance (do not remove a row whose suite is still red), the row was NOT removed; instead its reason/owner text was updated to describe the current, accurate gap, and a classification row (integration, invokes:verify-deploy.sh,run-all.sh) was added to the source-store copy of suite-classification.data. That suite's own lint resolves its subject 'deploy-tree-first', so the fix only takes effect once Phase 3's redeploy propagates it to the deployed tree; until then the suite remains correctly declared EXPECTED via the updated row rather than silently stale or silently removed. Re-verify and remove the row after redeploy if the suite then reports 0 failures standalone.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/suite-classification.data' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.

A single verify-deploy.sh full run's internal Gate 8 (gate8_run(), invoking tests/run-all.sh --fail-on-new) reported FAIL with exit 1 (meaning NEW_COUNT>0 for that one invocation), while 3 separate direct run-all.sh --fail-on-new invocations run immediately before and after it (same tree, same known-failures.txt) all reported 0 NEW, 3 EXPECTED, 193 passed/3 failed/196 total identically. No detail was captured for which suite was transiently classified NEW (verify-deploy.sh's gate8_run() does not log the roster unless FINDINGS=true, and this run did not set it). Plausible cause, consistent with this task's own Phase 1 finding: genuine ambient host contention from concurrently-running sibling /orchestrate dispatches on this shared machine, each potentially running their own full gate/test batteries at the same moment. Not chased further: the task's own acceptance bar (two full run-all.sh --fail-on-new runs reporting zero NEW) was independently satisfied by two clean runs taken back to back, and the anomalous run did not reproduce on a third direct run-all.sh invocation taken right after it.

Hand-off: test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh (the eighth suite named in this task's originating observation, deliberately excluded from this task's file_scope) still reproduces its symptom verbatim today: 14 passed, 1 failed, with the single failure 'baseline fixture is not clean (rc=1, gate20 finding lines=0) -- fixture setup is broken; later cases are unreliable'. Direct re-run (standalone) shows the specific rc=1 in THIS measurement was caused by this task's own then-uncommitted-to-deploy source-store edits (known-failures.txt, suite-classification.data, test-gate-lock.sh triggering doc-lint/manifest-drift gate failures in the fixture's own nested verify-deploy --max-cost moderate self-check) -- i.e. this particular occurrence is NOT independent evidence of the suite's general root cause, since it will clear once this task's own redeploy lands. However, per report 02's own finding (task 476's second research dispatch), the symptom was ALSO already confirmed reproducing independently of this task's edits, after record 423's closure (423 attributed the failure to a different root cause: an eager-load/baseline-drift byte-count issue, now fixed) and after a later commit (a4e32ff9e) that specifically touched this suite's fixture without resolving it. Record 423 is CLOSED/archived and cannot receive this new finding. This needs a fresh follow-up task -- not a hand-off to a closed record -- to investigate whether 'baseline fixture is not clean' is a genuine ambient-host-state/repo-state leak into the suite's own self-check (its nested verify-deploy invocation reading live, possibly-dirty repo state) independent of any one task's transient deploy drift.
